title: Flowise CSVAgent -- T1059 an attacker-controlled data URI segment escapes a Python string literal and reaches Pyodide's js bridge
author: WinstonRedGuard -- sigma plugin observed rules (derived from breach corpus)
description:
Vendor-disclosed detection for CVE-2026-69264 (GHSA-4j8x-x6v7-w9rq,
CVSS 9.9 CRITICAL), affecting Flowise's `CSVAgent` node.

`CSVAgent.run()` extracts a segment of the `csvFile` data URI by
splitting on `,` and interpolates it VERBATIM into a Python
bootstrap template (`base64_string = "${base64String}"`) before
handing the assembled string to `pyodide.runPythonAsync()`. Neither
of the two validators guarding this code path
(`validatePythonCodeForDataFrame`, `validateCustomReadCSVFunction`)
is ever applied to the bootstrap template itself. An attacker crafts
a comma-free segment that closes the Python string literal early,
imports the `js` module, and calls `js.eval()` -- which on Node.js
bridges to `globalThis`, exposing dynamic `import()` of Node built-in
modules (`fs`, `child_process`). This escapes Pyodide's WASM sandbox
entirely and executes as the Flowise host process. The trigger route
`POST /api/v1/prediction/:id` is whitelisted from auth when the
chatflow has no `apikeyid` set (the default for new chatflows), so
one authenticated plant reaches unauthenticated RCE on every
subsequent prediction request.

Detection logic flags a chatflow prediction request whose CSVAgent
`csvFile` data-URI segment contains a Python string-literal
terminator (`";`) followed by an `import js` statement -- the exact
string-escape-then-bridge-import shape this advisory's verified
end-to-end proof of concept (against a stock `flowise@3.1.2`)
demonstrates writes a proof file on the Node host.

Aggregated from 1 first-party vendor security advisory (FlowiseAI, via
GHSA, citing the exact source file and line numbers, a standalone
reproduction against real Pyodide, and independent verification
against a live `flowise@3.1.2` install with owner-uid confirmation),
fixed in Flowise 3.1.3 (verified via live GHSA lookup, 2026-09-04 -- the rule's original authoring predates the vendor's patch release; this note corrects a stale claim, not the detection logic itself).
